notes: Never got a 200, so no field-level declared-vs-actual diff is possible here — that whole axis is UNVERIFIED, not PASS and not DRIFT. Two things ARE established with confidence, from the contract text plus the setup calls, independent of the 500s: (1) What this capability actually does, despite its name: it is NOT scoped to a test case at all — there is no case_id/test_case_id parameter anywhere in its contract. It takes a project_id and a list of arbitrary tag WORDINGS, and reports which of those wordings are new vs already used somewhere on that project's test cases (a project-wide vocabulary check against a supplied list), not 'verify the tags on test case X' and not 'report case X's current tags'. Its declared mode ('read') matches its declared/guidance-stated effect ('Nothing is saved by this check') — no mode-vs-effect drift here, unlike batch 2's update_custom_field. (2) The endpoint itself appears broken in preprod right now: every invocation — with a mixed known/new tag pair, with an empty array (which the contract explicitly promises is valid), and with a single ordinary tag name — returned the same 500 Internal Server Error, verbatim. This is NOT the 'the product could not be reached' outage signature the brief calls out, and a sibling read (list_test_case_tags) against the identical project_id succeeded immediately with 200, so preprod and this project are reachable; the fault is localized to verify_test_case_tags's own handler. Tag residue for the record: created tag '__mcp-probe-tag-20260918a' (applied to TC-54457 / int 1972036, scratch folder 764138, via update_test_case), confirmed present in project PR-2005's test-case tag vocabulary via list_test_case_tags (count 1, page 1). This tag is disposable, account/project-wide residue and is a good candidate target for a sibling update_tag (rename) probe.
